newsitem.title: USA: Ind. Treasurer wants halt in new bond authorities.
newsitem.headline: Ind. Treasurer wants halt in new bond authorities.

text.p: Indiana Treasurer Joyce Brinkman has called for lawmakers to stop creating new bonding authorities, contending that their proliferation has cost taxpayers more than if the state had one debt-issuing agency.
"What alarms me most is that no one call tell you how much debt the state has because it is so fragmented among these little debt kingdoms," Brinkman said Tuesday in a statement.
The Indiana Constitution prohibits general obligation debt issuance, but makes no restriction on moral obligation debt, which the state pledges to pay, Brinkman said.

Brinkman said Indiana could resolve the problem by amending the state constitution to broaden prohibitions on debt issuance or consolidate all bonding authority to "keep a handle on the amount of debt issued."
